content.thinking:
I need to write the full file carefully in one pass, designing a hunched troll skeleton roughly 2.6m tall facing +Z, with hips as root, spine chain, neck, head, jaw, arms with shoulder/elbow/wrist/fingers, and legs using limb IK—planning out the coordinates for a standing height with head top near 2.5m.

Plotting joint positions: hips at [0,1.15,0], a spine chain curving up through chest to a hunched-forward head and neck base, then defining the neck-to-head chain parented off the spine tip, and sketching how the body mesh will loft around these bones.

For the paint, I'm designing a mottled skin texture blending olive-green tones with a lighter countershaded belly, then layering a mossy patch pattern over the shoulders using noise-based blending so moss covers roughly half the surface without overwhelming the base skin color.

Now I'm positioning the arms, placing shoulders wide and setting hand targets so the arms hang down and slightly outward with elbows bending back; I'm chaining shoulder-elbow-wrist joints and sweeping them with tapering radii, adding a rounded pauldron-like shoulder ball for bulk. For the hands I'm planning a scaled fist shape at the wrist with a few simplified fingers per hand to keep the joint count manageable.

Each finger is set up as a short curled chain of three points -- knuckle, mid, and clawed tip -- swept with tapering radii and dark spiked tips, parented off the wrist joint from the arm chain.

Still working out finger positions...

Now I'm setting up the legs, placing hip joints at either side with foot targets and leg segment lengths to compute the bend angles.

Adding toe spikes with claws and setting up radius tapering for the leg chain from hip to ankle.

Now I'm checking that the foot sphere sits flush with the ground, then moving to the neck and head joint chain, deciding whether to use two named joints for neck and head so the head tip acts as the aim target.

For the head itself, I'm positioning the skull sphere, a dark brow ridge rod above the eyes, and a flattened snout sphere, all placed relative to the head joint's world coordinates.

Now I'm figuring out the jaw joint and its chunky underbite shape, plus curved tusk geometry sweeping outward and upward from the lower jaw using catmull-rom spline points with tapering radii.

I'm deciding to keep the tusks flat ivory with a bone ring accent rather than gradient banding, then adding small spike teeth and simple glowing eye spheres with dark pupils near the jaw.

Now I'm shaping pointy spike ears with a smaller red inner spike, and scattering mohawk-style feather spikes along a crest line running from the top of the head back and down.

I'm varying the crest spikes by region (front, mid, back) with different lengths and using a darker tone for a second layer, then planning bone fetish details—necklaces of teeth and skulls, shoulder trophies, forearm wraps, and anklets—built as swept rope paths with hanging spike elements along curves.

Still working out the necklace path and torso width...

Still writing torso profile code...

Since joint planes risk degenerate cuts near the start, I'll switch to draping closed ellipse loops around the waist for the belt, which won't throw errors. For the loincloth, I'm planning hanging strip extrudes with jagged outlines positioned around the front and sides to create a ragged draped look.

Writing strip geometry...

Adjusting the loincloth strip positions to sit correctly against the torso ellipse, then planning cloth texturing with layered red/brown grain colors and a mossy fur mantle draped over the shoulder.

I'm working out the shoulder pelt as a flattened scaled sphere with grain-painted brown texture, plus scattering around 40 moss tuft cards with hanging frames across the pelt, shoulders, and knees for added decay detail. I'm also sketching a skull-building function that assembles a cranium sphere, jaw box, dark eye sockets, and horn, oriented outward via a local quaternion frame for the trophy skulls.

Now I'm defining the skull's local axes -- x sideways, y forward along the snout, z up -- and starting to shape the cranium as a scaled sphere within that frame.

I'm sizing skulls smaller for regular items and larger for trophy pieces, and deciding which bone joint each fetish item attaches to—hips for belts, chest for chest pieces, head for head decorations. Now I'm planning the necklace design: a rope drape with hanging teeth and claws, beads, a central skull pendant, and a bone disc with a spiral texture rendered as a flat cylinder with decal detailing.

For the belt I'm adding angled skull plates near the hips, fang trophies, and a tan bone ring made from a torus; the left shoulder gets a pelt with two skulls plus a horn spike while the right shoulder gets a ring of bone spikes. For the forearms I'm sketching rope wrap bands using a closed sweep around the arm with outward-facing bone spikes arranged in a ring, working out the right radius so the wraps sit properly against the forearm's chain geometry.

I'm placing two wrap bands per arm near the elbow area, mirroring the same wrap treatment at the ankle on the leg with slightly smaller bone spikes, adding a small dangling skull pendant at the left wrist, and considering simple thin braid sweeps near the mohawk base instead of beads to keep things cheap.

Now I'm detailing the mouth with a dark red interior and small fang spikes along the upper and lower jaw, then working through body musculature placement—pec bulges on the chest, shoulder spheres, and trapezius humps near the neck base—positioning each based on the torso's path coordinates.

Adding scattered warts and spine ridge spikes...

Now adding moss patches as flat textured cards on upper surfaces like shoulders and torso top, tinted white and kept to a reasonable triangle count. I should also enlarge the tusks, with two big lower tusks, then move on to shaping the eyebrows next.

Nose gets a pink sphere with dark nostrils, skipping the lower lip detail but keeping chin warts and cheek features. For the hand claws, I'm placing a dark spike at each fingertip using the finger path's end tangent direction to orient it properly. Finally I'm consolidating the color palette down to a limited set of flat named colors like bone, rope, red, brown, claw, eye, and mouth tones to stay under the material count limit.

Adding muddy feet with noise-based mud patches near the ground, pulling in the noise and paint helpers for the skin coloring logic.

Setting up color constants and a profile interpolation helper, then starting the build function with a rng-seeded builder and the hip joint placement.

I'm now thinking through the spine chain structure, deciding whether to parent it from the hips joint and working out the path points for spine1 through chest to get a natural forward hunch.

For the torso itself, I want coverage from pelvis up, so I'm separating the pelvis into its own scaled sphere skinned to the hips joint, then sweeping a tube along the spine chain with radius profile varying by position for the main torso shape.

I need to type the radius function return correctly so TypeScript accepts it as a fixed tuple instead of a generic array. I'm also reconsidering the belly bulge direction—since the sweep's normal points backward along the tube, I need to flip the shift sign so the offset pushes the belly forward instead of backward.

Now I'm setting up the neck chain parented to the chest tip joint, sizing its radius taper and giving it rounded caps with skin coloring. Moving on to the head, I'm placing the skull's world-space center and starting to define its width and height dimensions.

Still placing head parts...

Still building jaw and mouth structure...

Now I'm skipping the tongue and tusk base rings, and moving to the ears -- adding spike-shaped outer ears with darker skin tone, pink inner spikes offset forward, and considering a gold ring earring detail for each side.

For the mohawk, I'm designing an SVG flame-blade texture: a tapering spiky shape with a gradient running from dark red at the root to brighter red at the tip, plus a highlight stroke, with a second darker/wider variant planned for crest frames.

Now I'm plotting the crest curve as a Catmull-Rom spline along the head from front to nape, with sample points tracing the skull profile, then generating orientation frames along that path tilted slightly backward for each crest segment.

For the mohawk cards, I'm using tangent-based frames with a backward sweep bias, leaning them toward the flow direction, sizing them small and spiky, and arranging roughly 30 cards in two offset rows to thicken the strip, matching the taller reference mohawk height. The neck-to-head transition at the nape looks fine as is, so I'm skipping braids and instead adding a few dreadlock-style strands behind the ear using short downward Catmull-Rom sweeps with thin red-brown cylinders and bead accents.

Now I'm defining the bead placement along each dreadlock path at a few fractional points with a color list, then moving to the arms: a shoulder ball joint positioned near the chest profile where it overlaps the torso radius, with the arm chain parented to the spine and hanging slightly forward with a wrist target offset in z. I'm working out the sweep radii across the arm chain keyframes to taper it evenly from shoulder to wrist.

Next I'm adding bulge balls for the bicep and forearm by interpolating between joint positions with the lerp helper, then setting up the leg chain: hip joints positioned relative to the torso, with knee and ankle targets computed so the limb distance fits within the allowed chain length, and naming each joint with a side suffix for left/right distinction.

Now I'm placing flattened foot balls that touch the floor at y=0, adding a toe row of four small scaled spheres angled slightly downward with claw spikes pointing forward from the front of each foot.

Checking the ankle joint position against foot geometry so the toes and claws line up with the leg sweep. I'm also sketching in a knee pad bulge offset slightly forward and a thicker thigh bulge placed partway along the leg using an interpolated point, sizing it larger near the hip to match the broader sweep radius there.

Now I'm working through the leg's radius profile across hip, knee, and ankle, adding anklets, bone spikes, and wrapping the toes, then setting up a shared skin surface that merges the torso and pelvis parts so the belt paints correctly across both. I'm defining the belt as a looped ellipse path with drape and a rope-style sweep for the geometry.

Adding a second thinner belt layer, studs along the path, and placing a skull buckle by raycasting against the torso surface to find the front-facing attachment point...

Plotting necklace path coordinates...

Adjusting the collar into a ring of short outward-angled bone spikes near the neck base, checking that the placement stays within the chest cap radius so it doesn't collide with other geometry.

Now I'm adding a draped teeth necklace hanging down the chest surface using spikes of varying length, then positioning a skull pendant and a spiral disc pendant above it on the front-facing surface coordinates.

I'm designing the spiral disc texture as a bone-colored circle with a dark spiral pattern drawn in SVG, then considering a wooden totem hanging from the belt near the loincloth, weighing box geometry with a spiral decal against potential overlap with the loincloth strips.

For the loincloth itself, I'm laying out front and back strips in an arc with varied lengths and widths, alternating between red and brown cloth colors using grain-textured paints for subtle variation, with the strips hanging down from a starting height near the hips.

Resolving the outward direction for the strip thickness axis, I move to placing belt elements and then shoulder trophies -- adding a pelt with skulls and horns on one shoulder, positioning the skull meshes with specific offsets and orientations.

Now I'm figuring out the fringe around the pelt rim, arranging cards in a ring formation with manually computed frames so each hangs outward and down with a flat fur-strand texture.

I'm layering in moss and fur tufts using mixed brown-green textures, scattering moss cards onto upward-facing surfaces like the torso and shoulders with density and spacing controls, then adding warts and pec-shaped balls to flesh out the torso's front contours.

Adding belly, trap, and back hump balls to shape the torso's bulges, then starting a skull helper function that builds a frame at a given position and direction to construct horned or plain skull geometry.

Writing skull helper function...

Adding more facial details...

I'm skipping fangs on the skull for now, but adding more bone fetish details: ring spikes on the arm fang bundle, a bone hoop torus at the belt, and planning a dangling thighbone charm.

Still placing bones...

Now I'm sketching the eye details with glowing pupils as dark vertical slits positioned just in front of the eye sphere, planning the depth so the pupil peeks slightly beyond the eyeball surface.

Checking the eye and brow placement against the skull's ellipsoid surface math to confirm they sit just embedded into the bone at the right depth and height.

Now I'm positioning the snout ball and pink nose tip, then working out the jaw ellipsoid's span and front extent relative to the head, checking for a closed-mouth underbite with tusks protruding from the jaw sides, and sketching where the upper teeth spikes should hang down from the snout's lower edge.

Since those upper teeth would overlap with any lower teeth pointing up, I'm scaling the lower jaw to just a few small front teeth plus the tusks. I'm sweeping a curved path through a set of points to form each tusk, checking that the x-coordinates stay within the skull width, and setting the taper radii and color for the sweep.

Now I'm shading the tusks with a darker ivory band near the base before transitioning to the main ivory color, and applying the same skin tone to the head and hands. Then I'm switching to building the card textures, starting with an SVG for a tuft of moss made from a few curved blade paths in a green fill.

I'm defining the hide fur tuft with similar blade shapes but in brown tones, and skipping the idea of dripping red tassels for now. For the mohawk texture I'm setting up a vertical gradient from dark red at the base to bright red at the top, shaping the hair strand as a tapered path, and adding a lighter highlight stroke down the center for depth.

Adjusting the stroke width since the scaled viewBox made a thin highlight line look too faint at width 2, so I'm bumping it to 3 for visibility. I'm also deciding to skip extra ambient-occlusion shading on the skin for now and move toward composing the full file, aiming for a modest part count (~300) with triangle geometry kept simple, and picking flat rope colors instead of procedural grain textures.

Writing the ball helper function...

Still defining helper functions for building parts, fingers, chains, and palm placement...

Checking the wrist-to-shoulder vector length against the arm segment lengths to decide how much the elbow should bend backward, then setting up the chain function that builds the array of limb points.

Then I'm confirming ring() returns item points perpendicular to the tangent, which I can feed into catmull with closed:true to sweep a rope band around those frames.

Working out radius values along the arm at different t positions, interpolating between keyframe radii so the band and spikes match the limb's taper, then sizing spikes at ~.12 length and .03 radius tilted outward from the axis. I'm doing similar radius interpolation for the leg/ankle wrap at t=.85.

For spikes I'm calling a helper with base position, direction, length, radius, and bone color/options. I'm also scattering wart geometry (small spheres) across the torso surface, roughly 40 of them with slight embedding, and doing similar sweeps for arm segments at 6 per sweep. For moss, I'm considering scattering across torso and hump surfaces but avoiding applying it to the whole model since that would be too heavy.

I'm skipping tooth marks on the torso and finalizing by returning the model root. I'm double-checking that the lowest points (feet, claws, ankle tube) rest near floor level, and that overall height including the mohawk crest comes out around 2.9 units, which feels right for a large troll. I'm placing the pelvis ball joint and making sure the spine and hip joints don't collide in naming, then being careful to use every declared variable to satisfy strict typing. Now I'm adding a small wooden totem box geometry positioned near the chest.

I'm attaching a rope rod to hold the totem in place, then adding a spiral decal plane in front of it, reusing the existing spiral texture to avoid creating a new one. For the loincloth, I'm scattering hanging bone spikes along the belt path at alternating intervals using a counter to track index parity. I'm also writing a small helper function that casts a ray forward from a given point to find where it hits the skin surface, falling back to a default position if there's no hit, so I can accurately place things like the front skull decoration.

Now I'm figuring out placement for a chest pendant skull and a belt skull: positioning the pendant near the upper torso attached to a spine joint, and placing the belt skull slightly forward of the loincloth strips so it floats just above them without clipping. I'm also working out symmetric positions for a pair of smaller skulls flanking the belt on either side.

For moss, I'm using a cards helper to scatter small leaning, flowing moss patches across hit points, mainly on rim surfaces, while skipping extra hanging moss, side hair, and chin tufts for now to keep things simple. I'm finalizing the file structure and double-checking the loop spacing and random seed usage before writing everything out.
